title: A simple way to plan a weekend around Wesley Chapel
excerpt: One event, one outdoor stop, one new local spot. That's plenty for a good weekend.

body.text: A good weekend doesn't need a packed schedule. One local outing, a little time outside, and a stop at a nearby business can be plenty.
Start with one event

Pick something from the events page that suits your group. Before you go, check the organizer's page for start time, admission, registration, and parking. Some events need tickets in advance even when entry is free.
Leave room for an easy outdoor stop
A walk or a playground fits nicely before or after an event. Pick somewhere close to your main stop instead of adding a long drive. Bring water, check the forecast, and have an indoor backup in mind.
Make one local discovery
Try a nearby business you haven't been to yet. The directory is a good starting point. Just check opening hours with the business before you head out.
Keep the day manageable
One main destination, one optional stop. If you're heading into a neighboring town, check the drive time and don't book things back to back. A relaxed afternoon usually beats trying to do everything.

title: New to Wesley Chapel? Build your local shortlist
excerpt: You don't need to figure everything out in week one. Start with a short list of people you can call.

body.text: Settling in is easier with a few useful contacts and a couple of places you already know. You don't need to figure out everything in the first week.
Start with your everyday needs

List the services you'll actually use: home maintenance, pet care, personal care, places to eat. Browse the directory by what you need, then contact businesses directly to confirm their service area and availability.
Ask a few practical questions

Before booking, explain what you need and ask what's included in the price. For bigger jobs, get a written estimate and agree on timing, materials, and follow-up. A listing is a starting point for your own research, so choose whoever fits you best.
Find one place to spend an afternoon
A local park, a public event, or a regular coffee stop makes a new neighborhood feel like home faster. Check the events page and the park guides here.
Save what works
Keep a note on your phone with the businesses you liked, their numbers, and places you want to try next. Add a few options from nearby towns if they fit your routine.

title: 10 parks worth the drive in Pasco County
excerpt: Springs, salt marshes, a 40-mile trail, and a miniature train. All north of the county line.

body.text: Pasco has trails, playgrounds, and water for every kind of Saturday. Here are ten worth knowing.

items.name: Werner-Boyce Salt Springs State Park
items.text: Salt marshes and springs with kayaking, hiking, and bird-watching.

items.name: Starkey Wilderness Park
items.address: 10500 Wilderness Park Blvd, New Port Richey
items.text: Over 7,000 preserved acres for hiking, biking, and camping.

items.name: Anclote Gulf Park
items.text: A Gulf-front park with a fishing pier and sunset views.

items.name: Jay B. Starkey Wilderness Preserve
items.address: 10500 Wilderness Park Blvd, New Port Richey
items.text: Part of the Starkey system, with miles of trails through varied habitat.

items.name: Sims Park
items.text: Downtown park with a playground, splash pad, and riverside walk.

items.name: Crews Lake Wilderness Park
items.text: A miniature train ride, nature trails, and a lake for kayaking or fishing.

items.name: Suncoast Trail
items.address: Access at SR 54 & Suncoast Parkway, Odessa
items.text: Over 40 paved miles for cyclists and long-distance runners.

items.name: Anclote River Park
items.text: Sandy beach, boat ramp, and picnic pavilions.

items.name: Withlacoochee River Park
items.text: Riverside trails and a boardwalk, with canoeing and kayaking.

items.name: San Antonio City Park
items.text: A small-town park with a playground, sports courts, and shade.

cta.label: Plan the rest of the weekend

title: 10 parks worth the drive in Hillsborough County
excerpt: Boardwalks, mountain bike trails, and the Riverwalk, all south of the line.

body.text: From wetland boardwalks to waterfront piers, Hillsborough has plenty within reach of Wesley Chapel.

items.name: Lettuce Lake Park
items.text: An elevated boardwalk through wetlands, a canoe launch, and plenty of wildlife.

items.name: Alafia River State Park
items.text: 6,000+ acres of rugged terrain for hiking, riding, and mountain biking.

items.name: Flatwoods Wilderness Park
items.text: Miles of multi-use trail through wetlands and prairie, close to New Tampa.

items.name: Tampa Riverwalk
items.text: The downtown path along the Hillsborough River, linking museums, parks, and restaurants.

items.name: Balm-Boyette Scrub Nature Preserve
items.text: A quiet 1,000-acre preserve for hiking and wildlife photography.

items.name: MacDill Park
items.text: Bay views and picnic spots, with planes overhead from the base.

items.name: E.G. Simmons Regional Park
items.text: On the shore of Tampa Bay for fishing, kayaking, and picnics.

items.name: Plant Park
items.text: Shady downtown green space with historic landmarks on the river.

items.name: Hillsborough River State Park
items.text: Canoeing, fishing, and hiking along the river.

items.name: Ballast Point Park
items.text: A waterfront pier and boat ramp, and a good spot to watch the sunset.

title: The people behind our local businesses: share your story
excerpt: Behind every local business is someone who decided to build something. We want to hear from them.

body.text: Behind every local business is someone who decided to build something. We want to hear about the people doing that work around Wesley Chapel.
Business Spotlights go beyond a company name. What do you do? Why did you start? What do you wish locals knew about your work?
What makes a good story
Specifics. What you offer, where you work, and one thing that makes your approach personal. How you got started, or a lesson you learned the hard way, beats a list of slogans every time.
What to send

items: Your business name and a website or WCN listing link
Who we can contact, with permission to use their name
A short explanation of what you do and how it began
Your service area and public contact details
A photo you own or have permission to share, with credit

body.text: Put “Business Spotlight” at the start of your subject line. Submissions are reviewed for relevance and accuracy, and sending one doesn't guarantee publication. Any paid feature is clearly labeled.
